title: Reservation audit, tenant sandboxing, and adaptive burst safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a capacity incident on 2026-02-27 a single tenant’s sudden spiky workload and unbounded short-term bursts caused repeated eviction storms on two dedicated clusters. Symptoms included sustained tail latency increases, token-level cost spikes, and canaries failing the latency SLO.

Root cause analysis: Three contributing conditions aligned: (1) several small reservations were mis-sized relative to observed peak concurrency and KV-cache working set, leaving little buffer for transient load; (2) the tenant in question used high-concurrency, short-sequence batch requests which amplified GPU utilization variance and hot KV-cache churn; (3) the existing burst policy allowed large instantaneous token bursts without a smoothing window, which permitted the tenant to consume a disproportionate share of pooled burst capacity and trigger eviction-driven preemptions. Telemetry: top-10 offending tenant accounted for ~22% of burst tokens during the 18:04–18:22 window and correlated with a 4x increase in eviction events.

Impact: Multiple customers on the affected clusters saw degraded P50/P95 for generation routes (P95 latency regressed by ~500ms). Two Dedicated customers observed request failures and filed support tickets. No data loss.

Why this ticket: This is the consolidated post-incident action ticket to (a) audit current reservation sizing and correct misallocations, (b) implement tenant sandboxing/containment to limit short-term neighbor impact, and (c) introduce an adaptive burst smoothing mechanism plus safeguards that prevent a single tenant from draining pooled burst tokens in a few seconds.
acceptance_criteria: Reservation audit queries run and export produced; list of candidates for right-sizing created and prioritized
Tenant sandboxing prototype (cgroup-like GPU/slot limit + eviction threshold) merged to staging and validated under load
Adaptive burst smoothing implemented (sliding window token decay) with config knobs; default conservatively reduced
New observability: per-tenant burst score, eviction-rate alert, and a dedicated dashboard present in Console
Runbook updated with evacuation, rollback and postmortem links; canary rollout plan documented and approved
